questions.question: A user told your agent about an allergy in yesterday's session. Today the agent ignores it. What is the most likely cause?
options: The model forgot it overnight
Yesterday's conversation is not in today's context window, so the model never saw it
The temperature was too high
The model refuses to discuss allergies
questions.explanation: A model has no memory between calls. It only knows what your code puts into the current window.

questions.question: In the ContextBuilder, what is the difference between a section's priority and its order?
options: They are the same thing
Priority decides what survives a tight budget; order decides where the section sits in the prompt
Order decides what survives; priority decides the position
Priority sets the temperature for that section
questions.explanation: They are separate on purpose: the most important section is not always the one that should come first.

questions.question: At the very tight budget, the customer memory survived but the answer was still wrong. Why?
options: The memory was placed too early
The product facts were dropped, so the model knew about the allergy but not which kettle contains nickel
The task was dropped
The token estimate was wrong
questions.explanation: A constraint is only useful together with the facts it depends on. Dropping sections independently separated them.

questions.question: What does 'lost in the middle' refer to?
options: Agents that stop halfway through a task
Facts in the middle of a long context are used less reliably than facts near the start or the end
Tokens lost when a prompt is truncated
Messages dropped by a network proxy
questions.explanation: Liu et al. (2023) measured this; it is why position, not just inclusion, matters.

questions.question: Your agent gives a strange answer in production. What should you look at first?
options: The model's weights
The exact messages that were sent on that call, including what the context builder dropped
The user's browser
The average latency
questions.explanation: The answer is a function of the window. Log the kept and dropped sections so you can see what the model saw.

questions.question: Which statement best describes 'memory' in an LLM agent?
options: A special layer inside the model that stores facts
Text that your code stored earlier and puts back into the context window
The model's training data
The KV cache of the inference server
questions.explanation: Every memory technique is a write path into a store and a read path back into the prompt.
